boundary: Local Notes web, shipped Python CLI and real Textual PTY, generated Connect clients, real Go development BFF and current local store. The terminal segments replay actual terminal output with a high-contrast palette. No downstream gRPC or hosted run is asserted.

features.requirement: 001 US1 / 004 US1 / 005 US1 • create and open
features.remaining: Notes are returned by the Go BFF after browser reload.

features.requirement: 004 US2/4 / 005 US2 • typed validation and identity isolation
features.remaining: The primary film shows blank-title guidance and cross-subject refusal. The companion shows invalid title length/reference, absent identity, deadline, outage and a correlation reference. Cancellation, expired credentials and oversized body still need independent evidence.

features.requirement: 005 US3/4 • browser boundary and local startup
features.remaining: The running local client is visible. Cross-origin enforcement, production bundle identity exclusion and the one-command startup are verifier work.

features.requirement: 013 US1 • portable typed CLI and shared web round trip
features.remaining: The exact CLI-created reference opens in the browser. The companion shows the reverse browser→CLI read after a real local service restart, help, non-loopback identity refusal and typed JSON errors. Unfilmed command combinations remain in the CLI contract suite.
The shipped read-only TUI loads the CLI reference as the owner and denies the other subject.

features.requirement: 013 US3 • optional Android, iOS and desktop clients
features.remaining: Obtain an actual emulator, simulator, and supported-OS launch when the corresponding client ships. See #30, #31 and #32.
Land and run #60 and #59. The existing main CI desktop/mobile browser artifact uses its separate Connect fake.

features.requirement: Developer adoption, build, governance and deployment
features.remaining: The per-story appendix identifies the engineering checks. #20 owns the hosted release exercise and #21 the application-to-template lessons.
